units.Una PyG es uno de los informes más impor: A P&L is one of the most important reports for understanding a business.
units.Una Cuenta de Pérdidas y Ganancias (PyG): A profit and loss account (P&L) summarises a company’s revenue, costs and expenses over a period and shows what the final result has been.
units.En teoría, parece sencillo. En la prácti: In theory, it looks simple. In practice, a P&L can have many lines, levels and relationships between items.
units.Cuando la llevé a Power BI, mi reto no e: When I took it into Power BI, my challenge wasn’t simply getting the numbers to appear in a table. I wanted to be able to explore them without losing the financial logic behind each figure.
units.Antes de entrar en Power BI: ¿qué es una: Before getting into Power BI: what is a profit and loss account?
units.Una <strong>Cuenta de Pérdidas y Gananci: A profit and loss account (P&L) helps you understand how a business has performed financially over a period. Put simply:
units.Pero una PyG real tiene muchas más línea: But a real P&L has many more lines and levels. The final result depends on all the items behind it.
units.Por eso, cuando una cifra cambia, la pre: That’s why, when a figure changes, the interesting question isn’t just how much it has changed, but also which items explain that change.
units.Eso es precisamente lo que quería poder: That’s exactly what I wanted to be able to explore with this project.
units.Quería una PyG que pudiera explorar sin: I wanted a P&L I could explore without losing context.
units.Mi objetivo era construir un informe fin: My aim was to build a financial report that lets you move from an overview of the result to the detail that explains it. To do that, I worked with two main needs: looking at the P&L at different levels of detail, and understanding which items lie behind each result.
units.Así, el informe no se queda únicamente e: That way, the report doesn’t just show a figure: it lets you follow the path until you understand where it comes from.
units.Construí el modelo desde la lógica conta: I built the model from the accounting logic, not from the visual.
units.Antes de diseñar el dashboard, primero t: Before designing the dashboard, I first had to understand how the financial information was organised. A P&L isn’t just a list of numbers: each line has a meaning and is part of a structure of revenue, costs, expenses and results.
units.Por eso, primero organicé los datos sigu: That’s why I first organised the data following that logic, and then built the visuals on top of the model.
units.La estructura del modelo sigue la forma: The model’s structure follows the way a P&L is read.
units.El modelo permite analizar la informació: The model lets you analyse the information from different perspectives.
units.Puedo pasar del resultado a las partidas: I can go from the result to the items that help explain it.
units.Una tabla de hechos central y seis dimen: A central fact table and six dimensions.
units.Para construir el análisis utilicé una t: To build the analysis I used a central fact table related to six dimensions: PyG · Calendar, Accounts, Departments, Scenario, Organisations and Headers.
units.La tabla de hechos concentra los movimie: The fact table holds the movements I want to analyse, while the dimensions add the context needed to filter and group them.
units.Esta estructura me permite mantener la i: This structure lets me keep the information organised and analyse the financial items from different perspectives in Power BI. The idea was simple: the model should make the analysis easier, not limit it.
Two ways to read the same information.
units.Una PyG puede responder preguntas difere: A P&L can answer different questions depending on how you look at it. That’s why I built two complementary views.
units.<strong>PyG expandible</strong> — una vi: Expandable P&L — a view designed to start from the overall result and gradually open each level down to the detail. It lets me go from a total figure to the items that make it up without changing context.
units.<strong>Detalle con waterfall</strong> —: Detail with waterfall — a view focused on understanding how the different items contribute to the final result. The waterfall chart helps show which items increase or reduce the result on the way to the final figure.
units.No quería tener dos visualizaciones dife: I didn’t want two different visuals just for the sake of it. Each one answers a question: where am I? and what is explaining this result?

units.El total dice cuánto. La cascada ayuda a: The total says how much. The waterfall helps you understand why.
units.Pero esta cifra, por sí sola, no explica: But this figure, on its own, doesn’t explain what has happened. To understand it, I need to look at the items that contributed to reaching that result.
units.Ahí es donde entra el waterfall: permite: That’s where the waterfall comes in: it lets you follow visually how the different items add or subtract on the way to the final result.
units.Una cifra puede decirme <strong style=\": A figure can tell me how much has happened. The analysis has to help me understand why.
units.El mismo resultado puede contar una hist: The same result can tell a different story depending on how you look at it.
units.El resultado final es positivo y se encu: The final result is positive and sits 92.1% above budget.
units.Es la cifra que necesito para saber cuál: It’s the figure I need to know what the result has been.
units.La cascada añade el contexto necesario p: The waterfall adds the context needed to understand which items contributed to reaching that result.
units.Al combinar ambas vistas puedo pasar ráp: Combining both views, I can move quickly from the final figure to the detail that explains it.
units.El total responde al «cuánto». El detall: The total answers «how much». The detail helps answer «why».
units.Para construir el modelo, las medidas y: To build the model, the measures and the report’s visuals.
units.Para crear los cálculos necesarios para: To create the calculations needed to analyse the results and compare them with the budget.
units.Para preparar y transformar los datos an: To prepare and transform the data before using it in the model.
units.Para organizar las relaciones entre la t: To organise the relationships between the fact table and the dimensions.
units.Para representar la PyG de forma que fue: To show the P&L in a way that makes it possible to go from the overall result to the detail.
units.Lo difícil no fue solo el visual. Fue ma: The hard part wasn’t just the visual. It was keeping the meaning of every figure.
units.En una PyG, el signo de una cantidad imp: In a P&L, the sign of an amount matters. Revenue and expenses don’t behave the same way in the calculation of the result. If that logic isn’t kept correctly, a figure that looks right can end up telling the wrong story.
units.Por eso presté especial atención a cómo: That’s why I paid special attention to how signs were handled in the model, in the measures and finally in the visuals.
units.Este fue uno de los aprendizajes más imp: This was one of the most important lessons of the project: in a financial report, the number being right isn’t always enough. It also has to be shown the right way.
units.Una PyG que mantiene el contexto al camb: A P&L that keeps its context as the level of detail changes.
units.El objetivo final era conseguir que el u: The final aim was for users to explore the information without losing sight of the result they were analysing. From the P&L total down to the detail of each item, every level had to keep the same logic.
units.Este proyecto me ayudó a trabajar algo q: This project helped me work on something I think is especially important in Power BI: it’s not just about getting a report to work, but about making its numbers make sense when someone uses them to understand a business.
